name: Solar Industries India Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest commercial explosives maker (bulk and packaged explosives, detonators, initiating systems; ~26% volume share FY25, wallet share 20-23% with Coal India) with fast-growing defence (rockets, warheads, ammunition filling, pyro) and international explosives (Africa, Asia, Americas). Q2 FY27 revenue Rs 3,519 cr (+69%), EBITDA Rs 1,006 cr (28.6%), PAT Rs 617-650 cr (+79%); H1 revenue Rs 7,187 cr (+70%) vs FY27 guidance of Rs 14,000 cr (to be surpassed). Revenue mix Q2: defence 29%, international explosives 43%, domestic explosives 27%. Order book Rs 20,178 cr (defence Rs 17,568 cr). Announced all-cash acquisition of South Africa's Omnia Holdings for US$1.355 bn (Rs 12,951 cr) on 14 Sep 2026; FY28 combined target revenue >Rs 30,000 cr and EBITDA Rs 6,800-7,000 cr.

revenue_mix.geography: Africa, Asia, Americas, Europe (own plants + exports)

cost_structure.input: Other chemical / petro-derived RM, aluminium powder, packaging

exposures.mechanism: Defence is 29% of Q2 revenue (24% a year ago) and Rs 17,568 cr of the Rs 20,178 cr order book; FY27 defence revenue target >Rs 4,500 cr (Q2 only ~Rs 1,002 cr, so heavily H2-loaded). +10% domestic orders -> defence revenue +4% (domestic ~40% of defence book, estimate) = +1.2% total revenue at ~33% margin -> EBITDA +1.7%; EV/MCap 1.05; persistence 1.0 (multi-year contracts) -> +1.8; add growth-multiple (74x) sensitivity -> +3.

evidence.note: Defence 29% of revenue; order book Rs 20,178 cr of which defence Rs 17,568 cr; FY27 defence target > Rs 4,500 cr
MOFSL: defence to sustain higher growth; 43% revenue CAGR FY26-30

exposures.mechanism: Global ammunition/rocket demand lifts export orders (international explosives 43% of revenue; defence exports in the order book). +1 = defence exports 20% above plan -> defence export revenue +20% (~half of defence ~Rs 2,000 cr in FY27, estimate) = +Rs 400 cr = +3% group revenue at ~33% margin -> EBITDA +3.5%; EV/MCap 1.05; persistence 1.0 -> +3.7, plus rerating -> +5.

evidence.note: Higher defence and overseas contribution lifted margin 200 bp
International footprint via exports and overseas manufacturing

exposures.mechanism: Escalation raises ammunition and explosives demand (defence customers, mining security of supply) and international pricing, but also lifts fuel/AN/aluminium costs and disrupts shipping/Middle East operations. Net sign uncertain; defence skew gives a small positive: +1 -> defence order flow +5% (+1.5% EBITDA) vs cost +0.5% (-1.5% EBITDA); sentiment premium -> +1.5.

Domestic explosives are 27% of Q2 revenue; Coal India (wallet share 20-23%) and infra/tunnelling/roads are the buyers. +10% government capex -> domestic explosives volumes +4% on half the segment = +0.5% revenue; EBITDA +0.7% x1.05 x persistence 0.5 -> +0.4; plus defence-infrastructure linkage and multiple -> +1.5.

evidence.note: Market leader, 26% volume share FY25, wallet share 20-23% with Coal India
Domestic explosives supported by mining and infrastructure demand

exposures.mechanism: Power demand growth drives coal output and thus bulk-explosive consumption at Coal India/captive mines. +3 pp demand -> coal production +3% -> coal blasting volumes +3% (~15% of revenue) = +0.45% revenue; EBITDA +0.6%; x1.05 x 0.5 -> +0.3; multiple -> +1.0.

evidence.note: Domestic explosives backed by mining demand

exposures.mechanism: Ammonium nitrate (AN) tracks ammonia/urea-chain prices and is ~18% of sales (estimate: gross margin 54%, RM 46% of sales, AN ~40% of RM). +15% AN -> +2.7% of sales; Coal India and many private contracts carry price-variation clauses, ~80% recovered within a quarter -> 0.54% of sales unrecovered / 28.6% margin = EBITDA -1.9%; x1.05 x persistence 0.25 -> -0.5.

Overseas operations (South Africa, Zambia, Nigeria, Turkey, Latin America etc., model knowledge) sell explosives to miners. +1 pp regional growth -> volumes +2.5% on ~25% of revenue -> +0.6% revenue; EBITDA +0.9%; persistence 0.6 plus the Omnia SA footprint (+Rs ~13,000 cr deal) raising exposure -> +2.

evidence.note: Acquisition of South Africa's Omnia Holdings for ~US$1.355 bn / Rs 12,951 cr, all cash

exposures.mechanism: International explosives 43% and defence exports priced in USD/local currencies, with some imported AN/chemicals; and a new US$1.355 bn acquisition debt (financing mix not retrieved). +3% USD/INR -> +1.3% revenue translation (43% x 3%) at ~29% margin = EBITDA +1.4%, less imports -0.3% -> +1.1%; x1.05 x 0.5 = +0.6; USD-debt revaluation on Omnia funding offsets -> +0.5.

evidence.note: All-cash Omnia deal ~US$1.355 bn; funding structure not disclosed in the fetched article

exposures.mechanism: Interest cost Rs 172 cr TTM (Rs 55 cr in Sep qtr), set to rise sharply with Omnia (Rs 12,951 cr, all-cash; if ~70% debt at ~8% = ~Rs 720 cr/yr vs TTM EBITDA Rs 3,555 cr). +25 bp on ~Rs 9,000 cr floating debt (estimate) = Rs 23 cr ~ 0.7% of PAT; plus discount-rate effect on a 74x stock -> -2.

evidence.note: Interest Rs 41 cr (Jun-26) -> Rs 55 cr (Sep-26); P/E 74.4

exposures.mechanism: Modest direct cost link (fuel, petro-derived emulsifiers/packaging ~5% of costs), offset by geopolitical-demand linkage (defence/commodity-cycle co-movement). Empirical +1.22 (t +1.5) -> +0.5 after shrinkage; sign is not a cost channel and should not be double-counted with C_MIDEAST_CONFLICT.
Russia is a major AN/ammonia exporter; closer trade access/discounts lower AN prices: +1 -> AN -5% -> costs -0.9% of sales; recovered 80% via PV clauses -> EBITDA +0.7% x 0.5 -> +0.5.

evidence.note: Russia's share of global AN supply; not verified for Solar's procurement mix
